ca_milky_way_wall.blurb: Milky Way Wall is a tall granodiorite face on Shuteye Ridge, in the western Sierra foothills above Bass Lake and North Fork. It rises about 700 feet and is climbed by multipitch trad lines up runnels, cracks and knobby faces. There are eight routes, mostly in the 5.8 to 5.10 range, and the angle is gentler than the height suggests. The wall faces southwest, so it sits in shade through the morning and picks up sun in the afternoon. The base is reached on a cairned climbers' trail with real elevation gain, and the same trail continues on to the upper tier.

ca_missing_link_the.blurb: The Missing Link is a single monzogranite formation on Snow Bird Ridge, among the pinnacles of the San Bernardino Mountains near Lake Arrowhead. The rock stands roughly 50 to 60 feet tall, and the base is flat enough to settle in comfortably. It has eight trad routes: one around 5.9, a couple of 5.10s and most of the rest at 5.11. The walk in from the parking area follows a creek bed and is short, which suits a quick day, and the ridge sees little traffic.

ca_mushroom_boulder_6.blurb: Mushroom Boulder is the most prominent block in the farthest section of Idyllwild County Park, perched on the hillside above the campsites in the San Jacinto Mountains. Its uphill side holds the good problems, and one more line on the downhill side doubles as the way down; the remaining faces have little to hold. There are eight problems spanning V0 up to V8, with one at nearly every grade between, so a mixed group can find something each. The boulder is a short walk uphill from the numbered campsites at that end of the park, and the hillside has more blocks scattered around it.

ca_no_falls_wall.blurb: No Falls Wall is a monzogranite formation beside the Barker Dam loop in Joshua Tree National Park, the last large rock before the dam itself. A prominent high roof sits in the middle of the face. The wall faces north and stays in shade for most of the day, which helps in warm weather. There are eight routes, mainly cracks, most of them trad with a couple of top ropes, running from 5.8 up to around 5.11. Reaching the routes farther along the face means scrambling across the tops of large boulders. A flat area at the left end has room for short top-rope setups.

ca_north_dallas_40.blurb: North Dallas 40 is a conglomerate wall at Texas Canyon, in the high desert of northwest Los Angeles County between Santa Clarita and Agua Dulce. It is about twenty yards wide and sixty feet tall, tucked between the Lower East Side and Pangea Wall below the huge Elephant Head formation, and overhung by the tower called the Elephant's Ear. All eight routes are bolted sport lines, with most around 5.10, one near 5.8, one 5.11 and two 5.12s. Some of the rock is stained by bird droppings, and conglomerate here should be left to dry fully after rain.

ca_2_brain_block.blurb: Brain Block is a short, almost perfectly vertical granodiorite block in the upper part of Snowshed East on Donner Summit near Truckee. From a distance it looks blank, but up close it is covered in small edges, so the climbing is fingery and technical rather than powerful. Of its eight routes, seven are sport and one is trad, and the grades lean hard: mostly 5.13, with a few 5.11 to 5.12 lines and one easy trad climb. Several linkups connect the main lines. The approach is the same as for the main east face just below.

ca_3_gully_right_side.blurb: Gully - Right Side is the part of the Snowshed Wall's north face on the right-hand side of the gully when you face uphill, on Donner Summit. The granodiorite here sees fewer parties than the main wall next to it. There are eight routes, six trad and two sport, firmly in the harder moderate bracket: one around 5.8, a couple of 5.10s and five at 5.11. To get there, head around the right edge of the main wall.

_skipped.ca_mushroom_boulder: Williamson Rock is closed to climbing; only one page describes the boulder itself.
